solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Sounding alert to increase cut from apiculture

indicators.note: something cut from a word is taken out of it, so the letters for 'to increase' are removed from the longer word

blocks.note: apiculture is the keeping of bees
to eke is an old verb meaning to add to or increase

explanation.surface: A beekeeping warning about expanding the hives, with an alarm going off.
explanation.walkthrough: BEEKEEPING loses EKE from its middle (B-E-[EKE]-EPING) to leave BEEPING.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that is beeping is giving out short electronic tones as a warning signal.

clue.text: Truck’s back in to bulldoze thickets

indicators.note: the back of a word is its tail end, so only its final letter is kept
in tells us one piece goes inside the verb that follows it

blocks.note: to boss is to bully or push people around, as a bulldozer does
the final letter of truck

explanation.surface: A lorry reverses into a site to clear the scrub.
explanation.definitionFit: Bosks are small woods or clumps of bushes, an old word related to bosky, meaning wooded.

clue.text: Start of Easter needing agreement on age of Moon at Jan 1

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, which is all that is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of Easter
a pact is a formal agreement

explanation.surface: Church calendar-makers needing to agree on the lunar phase before fixing Easter.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is apt: the epact was used in calculating the date of Easter.
explanation.definitionFit: The epact is the number of days in the lunar phase on the first of January, used in computing church festivals.

clue.text: Voting I see extremely ominous signal from crowd

blocks.note: a poll is a vote
taken as written
the letter C is pronounced 'see'
ever so means extremely, as in 'ever so kind'

explanation.surface: A voter senses an ominous mood in the crowd at the ballot.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it POLL-I-C-EVER SO; 'extremely' looks like an indicator for outer letters but is the phrase ever so.
explanation.definitionFit: Pollice verso, Latin for 'with thumb turned', was the gesture of the Roman arena crowd condemning a defeated gladiator.

clue.text: French name of southern department

blocks.note: nom is the French word for name
o' is a shortened form of of, as in o'clock
S is the abbreviation for southern

explanation.surface: A query about what the French call a region in the south of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: The French context steers towards a French department, but the answer is the Greek term.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomos is a province or administrative division of modern Greece, comparable to a French département.

clue.text: Rebuffed swine with a large sword

indicators.note: to rebuff is to push back, so the following words are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: a suid is any member of the pig family Suidae
taken as written
lg is an abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Someone fends off a charging boar using a big blade.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole string SUID+A+LG is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The gladius was the short stabbing weapon carried by Roman legionaries and gladiators.

clue.text: Brass item protecting small metal plate

indicators.note: protecting something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps round another

blocks.note: a tuba is a brass instrument
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A brass object guards a little metal sheet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brass item' suggests metalwork but means a musical instrument from the brass section.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsuba is the metal guard plate between the blade and hilt of a Japanese sword.

clue.text: Spooner’s garbled sentence entertaining international maths student at Cambridge (12, two words)

indicators.note: garbled speech is jumbled, so these letters are mixed into a fresh order
to entertain is to take in a guest, so one piece is held inside the others

blocks.note: the name taken as written, used as anagram fodder
time is a prison sentence, as in doing time
I is an abbreviation for international

explanation.surface: A garbled remark by the famously tongue-tied Oxford don Spooner, with a foreign guest present.
explanation.walkthrough: Spooner's name signals a spoonerism, but here it is just seven letters to rearrange; I goes inside SENOROP before TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: At Cambridge, a senior optime is a mathematics graduate placed in the second class of the Tripos, below the wranglers.

clue.text: Pointed gun when unsheathed …

indicators.note: unsheathed means stripped of its covering, so the outer letters are removed and the middle kept

blocks.note: to gun someone down is to murder them; the inside of that word is kept

explanation.surface: A weapon is drawn and aimed, continuing into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Gun = MURDER, as in gun down; losing its first and last letters leaves URDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Urde is a heraldic term for a cross or ordinary whose ends are pointed.

clue.text: … cowboy’s upset gripping Colt

indicators.note: gripping something means holding it inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: to bother someone is to upset them
C is the abbreviation for colt in racing form

explanation.surface: A Western gunslinger is rattled while clutching his revolver.
explanation.walkthrough: Colt looks like the revolver; it is the young horse, abbreviated as in race cards. A cowboy here is a shoddy tradesman.
explanation.definitionFit: A botcher does poor, careless work, just like a cowboy builder or plumber.

clue.text: Before very early shifts worker’s home

indicators.note: shifts means moves around, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: A is short for ante, Latin for before
V is the abbreviation for very
taken as written, used as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A worker starting very early shifts before dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worker' and 'shifts' paint a factory scene, but the worker is a bee.
explanation.definitionFit: An alveary is a beehive, the home of the worker bee; the worker is a crossword-favourite for a bee or ant.

clue.text: Partner driven insane by heat leaving Turkey

indicators.note: something leaving a word goes out of it, so those letters are dropped

blocks.note: troppo is Australian slang for mentally unbalanced by the tropical heat
TR is the international vehicle code for Turkey

explanation.surface: A companion goes mad in the sweltering heat and has to leave Turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: TROPPO without TR leaves OPPO.
explanation.definitionFit: Oppo is British informal for a colleague, mate or opposite number, someone you work alongside.

clue.text: Flimsy trifle to collapse — what’s learned on reflection?

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so these words are read in reverse

blocks.note: a business that folds collapses
lore is knowledge that is learned and passed on

explanation.surface: A light dessert is set to sink, prompting thought about lessons learned.
explanation.walkthrough: Trifle looks like the pudding; here it means a thing of no importance.
explanation.definitionFit: Folderol is foolish nonsense or a showy trinket, a flimsy thing of little value.

clue.text: Ship left for India scuppering many a pirate vessel

indicators.note: one thing for another means swapping it in its place
to scupper is to wreck, so the word is broken up and rearranged

blocks.note: a sail is a ship, as in a fleet of twenty sail
L is the abbreviation for left
India is I in the radio alphabet
taken as written, used as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A ship heads for India and sinks many a pirate on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: In SAIL the I is replaced by L to give SALL; 'a' belongs to the definition, not the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A sallyman, or Sallee-man, was a Moorish pirate ship from the corsair port of Salé in Morocco.

clue.text: Missing one broken toenail that’s shed

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so a letter is left out
something broken is smashed up, so the letters are reassembled in a new order

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written, used as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A painful broken toenail that has been lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shed' reads as a verb for losing the nail; it is the noun, a hut.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a simple shed or outbuilding whose roof rests against the wall of a larger building.

clue.text: Fish dish with crust covering from cellophane bag

indicators.note: the crust or covering of a word is its outside, so only its two end letters are kept

blocks.note: the cod is a common sea fish
a pie is a dish
the first and last letters of cellophane

explanation.surface: A fish pie with a pastry top, bought in a cellophane bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crust' belongs to the pie in the surface, but it signals the outer letters of the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: A codpiece was a pouch or flap worn over the crotch of men's breeches in the 15th and 16th centuries.

clue.text: Sanction renouncing US pollution

indicators.note: renouncing something is giving it up, so those letters are dropped

blocks.note: to sanction a decision is to uphold or sustain it
taken as written

explanation.surface: Penalties imposed while the United States backs out of an environmental deal.
explanation.walkthrough: Sanction means approve here, not penalise: SUSTAIN minus US leaves STAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A stain is a discolouring mark, a form of contamination or taint.

clue.text: More tea, coffee and chocolate

blocks.note: mo is an old and dialect word for more
cha, or char, is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: A café order for another round of drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocha is a flavouring or drink mixing coffee with chocolate, named after the Yemeni port.

clue.text: Uncovered pickpocket after vintage pen

indicators.note: uncovered means stripped of its outside, so the end letters go and the middle stays

blocks.note: a cru is a wine of a particular vineyard or vintage
a diver is slang for a pickpocket; its inside letters are kept

explanation.surface: A pickpocket is caught after lifting a valuable old fountain pen.
explanation.walkthrough: A diver is old slang for a pickpocket. 'Pen' looks like a writing tool but is an enclosure, here one for trapping fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A cruive is a Scottish wicker trap or enclosure for catching salmon in a river.

clue.text: Photo in African capital reflecting front of head

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
a reflection is back to front, so the combined letters are read backwards

blocks.note: Tunis is the capital of Tunisia
pic is short for picture

explanation.surface: A snapshot taken in a North African city mirrors someone's forehead.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion happens first and the whole combination is then reversed, so the photo also ends up backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The sinciput is the anatomical term for the forehead and upper front part of the skull.

clue.text: Sailors safe drifting right around lake

indicators.note: drifting means moving aimlessly, so the letters wander into a new order
around means surrounding, so one piece goes about another

blocks.note: taken as written, used as anagram fodder
OK means right or correct
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Mariners drift safely around a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Right is OK, not R; it goes round L.
explanation.definitionFit: Seafolk are seafaring people, a collective term for mariners.

clue.text: Reprobate lasting no time

indicators.note: no means without, so the letter for the next word is taken away

blocks.note: something immortal lasts for ever
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A scoundrel whose appeal is short-lived.
explanation.walkthrough: Lasting no time reads as fleeting, but it means IMMORTAL without T. Reprobate is an adjective here.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprobate act or person is unprincipled and depraved, without moral standards.

clue.text: Pooh-pooh ego trips? Charming

indicators.note: something that trips stumbles and falls over, so the letters tumble into a new order

blocks.note: pish is an exclamation of contempt, as is pooh-pooh
taken as written, used as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at vanity trips, then decides they are rather charming.
explanation.walkthrough: Charming is the noun for casting spells, not the adjective meaning delightful.
explanation.definitionFit: Pisheog is Irish for sorcery or a spell, so it is the act of charming in the magical sense.

clue.text: Surgical instrument for cutting your bits off!

indicators.note: off can mean gone bad or wrong, so the letters are put into a different order

blocks.note: taken as written, used as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A surgeon's knife threatening to remove a patient's private parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bits off' reads as a cheeky threat; off is the signal to rearrange your bits.
explanation.definitionFit: A bistoury is a narrow surgical knife used for making incisions.

clue.text: Rouse once the morning’s nearly ended

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: a.m. stands for the morning
something over has ended

explanation.surface: Waking someone up when the morning is almost done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' marks the definition as an archaic word.
explanation.definitionFit: Amove is an obsolete verb meaning to stir up or excite, so it is an old term for rouse.

clue.text: Dense forest in Mosel valley

indicators.note: in tells us the letters are found inside the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Thick woodland in the German Mosel valley.
explanation.definitionFit: A selva is a tropical rainforest, especially in the Amazon basin.

clue.text: Childless if and only if smart

blocks.note: s.p. stands for sine prole, Latin for without issue, used in genealogy
iff is the logician's shorthand for if and only if

explanation.surface: A conditional statement about whether one is clever only when without children.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiff as an adjective is slang for spiffy, meaning neat and well-dressed.

clue.text: Parchment’s role to play attached to folio

indicators.note: to play with something is to move it about freely, so its letters are reordered

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for folio
taken as written, used as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: An old document's part in a play, attached to a page.
explanation.definitionFit: Forel is a kind of parchment or vellum used for book covers and cases.

clue.text: Match due to involve me

indicators.note: to involve is to include, so one piece is drawn inside another

blocks.note: a fee is a payment due
us is colloquially used for me, as in give us a go

explanation.surface: A sporting fixture that the speaker is expected to take part in.
explanation.walkthrough: Match is the thing you strike, not a game; due is a noun meaning payment.
explanation.definitionFit: A fusee is a large-headed match that stays alight in wind, used by smokers outdoors.

clue.text: Predict wood to be cut and cut

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the last letter is chopped off

blocks.note: a forest is a large wood
to hew is to cut with an axe

explanation.surface: A forecast that the woodland will be felled and chopped up.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'cut' trims FOREST; the second is HEW, which fits the woodcutting picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Foreshew is an old spelling of foreshow, to show beforehand or foretell.

clue.text: Further attempt to comb over

blocks.note: red is a variant spelling of redd, Scots for to tidy or comb out
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: Someone tries again to arrange a comb-over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comb over' looks like the bald man's hairstyle, but the words split: RED then O.
explanation.definitionFit: A redo is a second go at something, a repeat effort to get it right.

clue.text: Thatchers topping frail structure that is outside of Ross

indicators.note: topping means taking off the top, so the first letter goes
the outside of a word is its two ends, which alone are kept

blocks.note: a shell is a thin, fragile structure
i.e. stands for id est, that is
the first and last letters of Ross

explanation.surface: Roofers removing the top of a flimsy building in Ross.
explanation.walkthrough: Topping in the surface fits roofing, but it means beheading SHELL to HELL.
explanation.definitionFit: Hellier is a dialect word for a slater or roofer, someone who covers a building, here equated with thatcher.

clue.text: Old salve, balmy aromatic?

indicators.note: balmy plays on barmy, meaning crazy, so the letters go mad and are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written, used as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: An old fragrant ointment, smoothing and scented.
explanation.walkthrough: Balmy suits a fragrant salve but stands in for barmy. Aromatic is a noun here, a fragrant plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Lad's love is southernwood, a fragrant shrubby wormwood grown as an aromatic herb.

clue.text: See me, a little elderly, round Zambia?

definitions.text: See me, a little elderly, round Zambia?

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so one piece wraps around another
a little of a word is just a bit of it, here its opening letter

blocks.note: taken as written
Z is the international vehicle code for Zambia
the first letter of elderly

explanation.surface: A slightly aged person introducing themselves somewhere in southern Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: ME goes round Z, then E follows; the whole clue also describes an old person in East Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Mzee is a Swahili term of respect for an old man or elder, used across East and central Africa.

clue.text: Gorge chump of pork, dessert about to follow

indicators.note: the chump is the thick end of a loin, so only the end letter is kept
about means turned round, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: the last letter of pork
a fool is a dessert of fruit puree folded into cream

explanation.surface: Someone stuffs themselves with a pork chop and then pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: Gorge looks like a verb for overeating, fitting the meal, but it is a ravine.
explanation.definitionFit: A kloof is a South African term for a deep ravine or wooded valley.

clue.text: Chap’s skinned after claim revolving around tax

indicators.note: something revolving turns round, so the word is read backwards
skinned means having its outside removed, so only the middle is kept

blocks.note: to bag something is to claim it, as in bags I
feller is slang for a chap; the inside letters are kept

explanation.surface: A chap is fleeced by a revolving tax claim.
explanation.walkthrough: Bag means claim in the schoolchild's 'bags I'; feller is informal for a chap, and skinning it strips its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The gabelle was a hated salt tax in France before the Revolution, and more generally any excise tax.
